input.rationale: Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the operative access/use grant, but it runs to "the Company" alone: Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not covered, and there is no written-notice mechanic to add them. That is a material term of the fallback (affiliate coverage at minimum on written notice) left unmet. The silence is not neutral, because Section 10.3 (p0063) provides that "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement," which affirmatively excludes our Affiliates and contractors from the granted rights and leaves no path to add them — the rule's walk-away trigger. Section 10.3 is also only a standard binding-effect/successors-and-assigns clause; it confirms the Agreement inures to successors but does not grant an affirmative right to transfer the licence in an M&A transaction, so it weakly supports the second fallback element and cannot cure the missing affiliate coverage. Redline (validated, ok:true) extends the Section 1.4 grant to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and carves them, plus an express successor transfer right, out of the "no other person" limitation in Section 10.3, with the written-notice approach offered as a fallback. The licence is not stated to be revocable at HDI's discretion, so no change is needed on revocability.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access/use grant to the Company's Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf, and carve them (plus a successor transfer right) out of the "no other person" limitation in Section 10.3.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the access and use rights in Section 1.4 to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, since our group and outsourced providers operate the Site day to day, and carved them out of the "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" limitation in Section 10.3, which would otherwise strip those rights. We also confirmed the licence transfers to a successor in a merger or sale of assets to protect transaction continuity; if preferred, we can instead cover Affiliates and contractors upon written notice to HDI.
